subject: Persistent 5xx/429 surge — edge translation bottleneck affecting Lumena Pay production
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@lumena-pay.com>
To: david.kim@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Major production errors — sudden 5xx/429 spikes and timeouts since 09:00 PDT

David / Marissa,

We're seeing a production-wide surge of 5xx and 429 responses to Redwood endpoints starting ~09:00 PDT this morning. Latency climbed from our baseline (~120ms) to sustained 1.2s+ and throughput dipped by ~35%. Retries from our side have amplified the issue — we briefly hit request retries in the hundreds per minute which appears to be tripping upstream connection limits.

Attached: error-sample.log and a short pcap of an affected host. Key observations:
- 5xx responses (502/504) concentrated across multiple request paths to the dedicated endpoint (dedicated-us-west-2).
- Repeated connection resets from the remote NAT address; some sequences show asymmetric source translation.
- Client-side backoff didn't reduce attempts fast enough; we had a retry storm from 09:05–09:20.

This is customer-impacting — transactions are failing and settlement jobs are delayed. Please advise immediate remediation steps and whether you can fail over traffic to hosted endpoints while you investigate. We can join a bridge now.

Thanks,
Elena Soto
Head of Infrastructure, Lumena Pay
Attachments: error-sample.log (text), pcap-snippet.zip (pcap)
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@lumena-pay.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-11T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Major production errors — sudden 5xx/429 spikes and timeouts since 09:00 PDT

Elena — thanks for the quick heads up and for the logs. We're opening an incident and standing up a bridge.

Immediate actions:
1) I'm pulling in Networking and Serving runtime (Jonas) to triage NAT/VPC translation and connection-tracking saturation.
2) Marissa, can we authorize a temporary failover to the hosted API for critical settlement routes? Lumena will need routing instructions.
3) Please keep sending examples of failing requests (x-request-id), sample timestamps, and which region/route these originate from.

I'll update in the bridge within 15 minutes.

— David
David Kim
Director, Account Escalations, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: david.kim@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-11T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Major production errors — initial triage (NAT translation / conntrack)

On Sun, Apr 11, 2027 at 09:24, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai> wrote:
> David — thanks for the quick heads up and for the logs. We're opening an incident and standing up a bridge.

Quick summary of what I see after initial reads and a short packet capture: 
- Multiple VPC peering sessions between Lumena's VPCs and their Dedicated cluster show transient route flaps around 09:00 PDT. Route flap correlated with a spike in SYN retransmissions.
- The Dedicated NAT gateway (internal-managed SNAT) shows source port exhaustion and fast churn of ephemeral ports as retries from client side increase. This caused asymmetric SNAT mappings for a subset of flows; the backend closed some connections with 502/504.
- Firewall connection-tracking table hit a high-water mark and started dropping new entries for established-but-translation-needed flows, which surfaced as timeouts then 5xx responses from our runtime.

Attached: debug-trace.txt (local connection-tracking counters and kernel logs).
Interim mitigations we've enacted:
- Increased SNAT port pool temporarily on the affected nodes.
- Applied a more permissive conntrack timeout for established flows on the Dedicated edge for Lumena's subnets.
- Enabled a short-term token-bucket rate limiter on the Dedicated front proxy to slow retries and avoid immediate conntrack re-exhaustion (will add small latency but should reduce 5xx amplification).

Next steps (immediate):
1) Request Lumena to throttle client retry logic for 30m or accept a brief hosted failover while we stabilize.
2) We're starting a deeper trace to identify whether the VPC route flaps are on the customer side (BGP/GTW) or our peering config. I've opened SUP-12345 for tracking.

I'll post updates here as we see telemetry.
— Jonas
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@lumena-pay.com>, david.kim@redwood.ai
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Major production errors — escalation and short-term plan

Elena — thank you for patience. We're escalating this to leadership internally to approve a short remediation plan while the Networking team completes the root cause investigation.

Proposal (needs customer sign-off):
- Step 1 (0–30m): Lumena routes high-value settlement traffic to Redwood Hosted API (we will prioritize capacity and pin requests to reduce tail latency). Redwood will provide a simple DNS CNAME and routing instructions.
- Step 2 (30–120m): Networking performs configuration hardening on Dedicated (SNAT pool expansion + conntrack tuning) and validates route stability with a controlled traffic ramp.
- Step 3 (within 24h): Post-mortem and permanent config recommendations; if issue traces to peering/BGP on the customer side we will coordinate a joint maintenance window.

Ask for Leadership: temporary credit for downtime window and approval for burst capacity on Hosted to carry the customer while we stabilize Dedicated.

Elena, please confirm whether you can perform the DNS/CNAME change for the settlement endpoints and we'll coordinate the exact CNAME and TTL.

— Marissa
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@lumena-pay.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-11T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Incident update: mitigation applied and next steps (SUP-12345)

Elena — final update for the day.

What we changed (completed):
- Increased SNAT ephemeral port range on affected Dedicated nodes (reclaimed by 09:30 PDT).
- Adjusted conntrack ttl and high-water thresholds to avoid premature drops for established flows.
- Enabled a short-lived token-bucket limiter at the front proxy which reduced retry amplification; 5xx/429 rates dropped ~85% by 10:15 PDT and latency returned to ~150–220ms.
- Coordinated with Lumena to move critical settlement traffic to Hosted for a 2-hour window while we validate stability; thank you for the quick DNS change.

Open items / next steps:
- We will run a joint packet-level validation with Lumena and GCP Networking tomorrow at 09:00 PDT to determine whether the route flap originated in the customer's upstream or the peering config.
- Post-mortem will be published within 72 hours and will include permanent config recommendations and any credit/compensation details.

Attachments: lumena-maup-ack.pdf (customer-signed acceptance to hosted failover).

Thanks for working with us on this. I'll keep SUP-12345 updated and will loop in execs if we need longer outage credits.

— David
Director, Account Escalations, Redwood Inference
